subject: Evidence extract spec for legal review — access logs (who/what/when)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@medicahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: audit log exports we discussed — quick recap and next steps

Hi Lisa,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciated the context on Medica Health's audit and legal timeline. Short recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with Legal/Procurement timelines: 

What we covered (summary):
- You need a chronological "who/what/when" export for user access to PHI-related endpoints (read/write, model interactions) for the previous 18 months.
- Export must indicate actor identity (user id, service accounts), email when available, timestamp (UTC), resource type, resource id, action, and request_id/session_id for correlation.
- Delivery formats: preferred is CSV with a companion JSON schema or newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) if retention/size makes CSV impractical.
- Retention and access controls: you asked for a retention policy map and audit trail proving exports were generated from immutable logs.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We'll produce a small sample CSV (30–50 rows) showing the schema and typical values by 05/20 EOD PT.
2) Our security team will provide an "evidence extract spec" document describing extraction window, timezone, hashing/PII handling, and checksums for integrity.
3) Legal will receive a signed statement of export provenance and retention policy summary.

Marissa/Rishi — can you confirm you can produce the sample CSV and the spec doc by Thursday 5/20? If there are any limitations (e.g., max lookback for full raw logs vs. aggregated traces) flag them now so we can build them into the delivery.

Lisa — if Procurement/Legal want different fields or a different file format, let us know here and we will adapt.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs: none in this message

From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@medicahealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Medica Health Legal <legal@medicahealth.com>, procurement@medicahealth.com
Date: 2027-05-19T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: audit log exports we discussed — quick recap and next steps

Hi Naomi — thank you for the recap, that looks right. A couple of clarifications from Legal/Procurement side: 

- The export must contain an immutable timestamp and the original request_id; we need to be able to correlate to our internal incident tickets.
- For actor identity, we need both user_id and any external SSO identity (if available). If an actor is a managed service account, please indicate that explicitly.
- For PII: any fields that contain email addresses must be delivered in a reversible-hash (we will accept SHA-256 with salt) and you must provide the salt handling policy.
- We will need the first sample by 05/20 so our legal counsel can start review.

I attached Medica_Data_Request_20270519.pdf which has our minimal legal checklist.

Can you also include a suggested retention/restore SLA for exports (e.g., how long you keep generated extracts available to re-download)?

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Gomez
Head of Security Operations, Medica Health
lisa.gomez@medicahealth.com

Attachments: Medica_Data_Request_20270519.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: need export spec and hashed-email approach for Medica (legal asks)

Ben/Rishi/Marissa — looping you in with Legal's asks (see Lisa's note). Action items: 

- Rishi: can you prepare the sample CSV (30–50 rows) using the schema below and include both plain actor_email and a SHA-256(salt+email) column? If we cannot include plaintext email in delivered exports, include a mapping file in a secure location and note that mapping access is restricted.

Suggested CSV schema (columns):
- event_timestamp_utc
- actor_id
- actor_email (nullable or hashed depending on policy)
- actor_email_sha256
- actor_type (user/service)
- resource_type
- resource_id
- action (read/write/execute)
- request_id
- session_id
- ip_address
- user_agent
- model_variant
- token_count
- retention_flag

- Ben: security note — confirm the checksum approach (SHA-256 over the file) and whether we can sign with our internal key for provenance. Also confirm how long we keep generated extracts for re-download and whether we can stage them in the customer's preferred region (us-east-1).
- Marissa: please coordinate HubSpot updates and mark next touch for 05/21.

If there are any platform limits (e.g., max rows we can extract in a single job or lookback >12 months requires a special request), call them out. I will respond to Lisa once we have the sample + spec.

Thanks,
Naomi

Date: 2027-05-20T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence extract + sample CSV (attached) and next steps

Hi Lisa — attaching the sample extract and the internal spec doc for Legal review. Summary of what we attached and what to expect: 

Attachments (stubs):
- access_log_sample.csv (CSV, ~18KB) — 40 rows. Columns match the schema we discussed. actor_email column is present but redacted; actor_email_sha256 contains SHA-256(salt+email) values.
- evidence-extract-schema.md (MD, 4KB) — describes extraction window (UTC), timezone handling, file checksum (SHA-256), signing approach, and retention behavior.

Key notes:
- Extraction window: we produced a sample from 2026-11-01 to 2027-05-01. For full 18-month extracts, we can run a bulk job; note that lookback over 12 months will spin a long-running export job (estimated 4–12 hours depending on volume).
- Provenance: each exported file includes a signed manifest (SHA-256) and a job id. We can provide the manifest and job id for audit.
- Hashing: we used a customer-unique salt that is stored in our KMS and is only used to compute the SHA-256 for exports. We can provide a statement describing salt management but will not disclose the raw salt.
- Re-download retention: generated extracts are available for re-download for 30 days by default; we can extend to 90 days for enterprise customers under contract.

Next steps:
1) Lisa/legal: review the sample and schema, and confirm whether the hashed-email approach meets your reversible-hash requirement. If Legal requires reversible encryption rather than a salted hash, flag that — we'll need to coordinate KMS access and an SLA for key retrieval.
2) Ben/Rishi: assuming Legal is fine with the hash, plan for a full 18-month export job. I'll schedule a kickoff with Medica for 05/24 to agree on timing and region.

Lisa — please confirm receipt and whether Legal wants additional fields in the export.

Thanks,
Naomi

Attachments referenced: access_log_sample.csv, evidence-extract-schema.md
